CRM.rationale: Salesforce presents a compelling but not unambiguous value case. The franchise is dominant (#1 CRM globally, 20% market share, 95% recurring revenue) and the AI pivot is gaining real traction (Agentforce $1.2B ARR, tripling YoY). Q1 FY2027 showed accelerating revenue (+13.3% YoY to $11.13B), strong earnings growth (EPS +52.2% YoY to $2.42), and exceptional cash generation ($6.70B quarterly OCF). The valuation is deeply compressed — PE of 16.5x is at the floor of its 12-month range (16.5–57.4x), and the 6.1% earnings yield exceeds the 10-year Treasury by 164bps. The $25B ASR reducing share count by ~10% is a meaningful capital return catalyst. However, the balance sheet has deteriorated dramatically (debt from $8.44B to $39.28B, likely Informatica-funded), organic growth is decelerating to ~7% ex-FX, and legacy segments (Tableau, Marketing/Commerce) are softening. The seat-erosion risk from AI is a genuine structural concern. The PE compression appears to overstate the risk given cash-flow coverage of debt service, but the unmodeled acquisition risk and organic deceleration prevent a higher conviction score. The near-term catalyst of Q1 earnings beat (non-GAAP EPS $3.88 vs $3.12 consensus) and raised FY2027 guidance provides modest support, though the stock's failure to rally on the beat signals persistent market skepticism.

Non-GAAP EPS of $3.88 crushed consensus of $3.12; non-GAAP operating margin record 34.8%
Stock at $151.78 near 52-week low of $149.80, down ~45% from highs despite earnings improvement
